newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's AVIC plans US$500 mln HK shr listing - paper.
newsitem.headline: China's AVIC plans US$500 mln HK shr listing - paper.

text.p: Aviation Industries of China (AVIC) plans to raise US$500 million through Hong Kong listings of its car, motorcycle and civilian business operations next year, the South China Morning Post reported on Monday.

The daily quoted AVIC's chief economist Du Jinling as saying the company, which controls production of civilian and military aircraft in China, was expected to need at least US$1.0 billion in foreign investment in the next five years.
At least half of the total foreign investment needed would come from the listings in Hong Kong, Du said.

The Post said AVIC planned to group its car making, car parts and motorcycle units for listing, including Songhuajiang Auto and Changhe Auto factories which produce passenger and freight vans, and Nanfang and Jinchen Motorcycle factories.
The company would also consider listing some of its other businesses such as its aircraft manufacturing businesses, the daily said.
US investment bank JP Morgan is advising AVIC on the flotations, the paper said.
JP Morgan was not immediately available for comment.
